issues.subject: Axios Pro Rata: Field of Dumb

themes.theme: Anthropic sets all-time VC round record
themes.summary: Anthropic raised $65b Series H at $965b post-money (led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia), leapfrogging OpenAI's valuation; separately Apollo/Blackstone are syndicating a $36b private-debt deal to fund Anthropic's custom chip purchases from Google.

Groq is raising up to $650m from existing investors after its $20b Nvidia chip-licensing deal (which paid out investors and saw senior staff depart), relaunching as an AI inference neocloud under new leadership -- floated as a potential new AI-market transaction template.

themes.theme: Big Pharma redeploys GLP-1 riches into vaccines
themes.summary: Eli Lilly agreed to pay up to $3.8b for three vaccine developers (Curevo, LimmaTech, Vaccine Co.) covering shingles, bacterial pathogens, and Epstein-Barr virus -- a swing back toward infectious-disease prevention.

themes.theme: SpaceX IPO liquidity debate frames the AI mega-raise wave
themes.summary: Axios argues SpaceX's rumored up-to-$80b IPO, alongside potential Anthropic/OpenAI mega-offerings, still wouldn't approach 2021's IPO-proceeds share of market cap -- public/private markets seen as deep enough to absorb it.

themes.theme: PE recommits to legacy consumer & industrial brands
themes.summary: Arsenal Capital bought majority of Velcro Cos.; Fertitta Entertainment (Golden Nugget) agreed to buy Caesars Entertainment for $5.7b; AkzoNobel rejected a €12.49b bid for itself while pushing ahead with its own $9.2b Axalta takeover -- consolidation logic running in multiple directions in industrials/consumer.

Quantinuum, Innio, Entrata, Doncasters, Applied Aerospace & Defense, Safepoint, Sunshine Silver, and others all set terms or filed this week, while ProLogium and Newcleo took the SPAC route -- signalling the IPO window remains wide open into the summer.
